source: Citadel Taskmaster, strike 486681 on event 485484, 2026-11-11 15:34 PST
history: #564 (more test files at once on CI) was stress-testing CI by pushing land/564-probe-* branches back to back; their runs share tests.yml's concurrency group citadel-tests with real lands. land.sh waits for the desktop CI run on the commit it lands and falls back to the full suite on perigee, which sends Cara an alert, when that run doesn't go. #553's ef38a0f (23:26Z) and #568's a2b0824 (23:30Z) both show 'cancelled' in the Actions list.
message: Just got a notification that CI fellback to perigee, whats up?

facts.result:
retro log, land.md 2026-11-11:
land ticket/553 ef38a0f: no runner started the job within 90s (pending behind a land/564-probe run in progress); land.sh cancelled its run; CI FALLBACK
land ticket/568 a2b0824: same, behind the next probe; CI FALLBACK
facts.why: land.sh cancelled its own pending runs at its 90 s wait; GitHub didn't

right: Read the lands' retro log or output (or land.sh's CI wait) before naming the mechanism: each land's run sat pending behind a ~2 min probe already running and land.sh cancelled it at its 90 s runner wait. Tell #564 to stop the probes, without claiming GitHub cancels pending runs.
wrong: Inferred from the 'cancelled' status that GitHub keeps only one pending run per concurrency group and each probe push cancelled a land's waiting run, and told both Cara and #564 so.

checks.why: read the lands' own log for why the runs were cancelled before naming the mechanism
the claim the strike took back
